transcript.content: XFM's Ricky Gervais talks to Bono.
I'm Ricky Gervais and I'm talking to Bono off U2.
Hello there, thanks for inviting me.
Alright Bono, sorry I don't know your surname.
I haven't got one.
Do you like XFM?
I bloody love it.
Is it because we play R.E.M., Eminem, Radiohead and Dr. Dre?
It is, and also of course you play some of my songs, U2 lead singer of. I've heard in the past on the station you've played Pride In The Name Of Love.
Pride in the name of love, before you break my heart.
Love that one.
And I imagine Christmas time you'll probably be playing All Is Quiet On New Year's Day. Oh, of course it is, all the shops are shut, there's no buses running. That's what I wrote it about, Rick.
Thanks very much.
Bono, I don't know your surname.
I haven't got one.
Ricky Gervais, this Saturday from 1. Yeah, with Steve Merchant, just, you know, say that.
104.9, it's The Ricky Gervais Show.
With Steve Merchant.
We've got some great bands coming up, we've got Ash, R.E.M., we've got Strokes, we've got Weezer, the usual stuff.
So listen, can I mention to you about the Aberdeen Angus Steakhouse?
Go on.
It's the one that you literally can see from this building.
Well, don't mention it.
What do you mean? There's loads of them.
No, but if they think you go there, then, you know, people will go there and we could charge them big advertising for that. We're losing revenue, hand over fist.

No, we, um, I don't know if anyone's ever been in an Aberdeen Angus Steakhouse. For those that haven't really spotted them, they're those places that have always got the kind of red velvet seating, and it's like, it's just sometimes I think they're just called like a steakhouse.
Yeah.
So we went in there and we ordered the food, and I gotta say this, the Aberdeen Angus Steakhouse, I'm embarrassed for the people that work there. They were embarrassed.
You can't say this.
No, it's not libelous, this is my opinion, it's like a restaurant review. It is. I'm like Michael Winner.
Oh, I'm gonna do that from now on as well, write that one down, restaurant review, yeah, I can do that.
But, um...
Got my film review coming up, don't forget that.
Oh, I look forward to that.
But, um, so we went in there and we ordered, I think my starter was prawns, right, in breadcrumbs.
Oh, that's the...
I ordered them and it...
That's the poshest thing you can do.
It was about four quid.
Four pounds. Like, for prawns. I swear to God, Rick, there were three prawns on a plate.
You're joking.
I'm not joking, three prawns on a plate, and a bit of grotty lettuce.
Oh, my God.
It was shameful.
And they brought us, we ordered sort of steak or something, it's the worst place, everything you've gotta pay for, napkins, salt and pepper, everything, it's ludicrous.
Seat higher.
It's absolutely, it literally was awful, right, and there was about ten of us, it cost about two hundred quid.
You're joking.
I don't know what the meat was, I don't know...
Can I just say, that is only twenty pounds each.
I don't think it was meat.
That is London.
I don't think it was meat, I think they'd literally crawled into the McDonald's next door, they were just stealing the meat waste from there.
It was unbelievable.
That is libelous, but it's obviously ironic, he's joking.

No, I'm saying that this is my hypothesis, Rick, it was an absolute travesty. I don't know how they get away with it, I don't know who goes back there, I thought restaurants were building a reputation on people who return and eat again.
And as you say, it's probably American tourists.

I like the way they look like a bingo hall, because you're walking past, it's huge, with a big opening, you can see exactly who's eating there from the beginning, do you know what I mean? And it's always like a couple of parents and some kids who are obviously not enjoying themselves.
Yeah, they're fat kids as well.
They're 14.
I know, yeah, yeah, yeah.

And after the Aberdeen Angus Steakhouse, we were very annoyed. And as is obviously the tradition on a stag night, it was, well, we'd have to go to a strip club. Now, I'm not a fan of that sort of thing, I have to say, unlikely, as that may seem. And I've never been to one before, and we tried to get in Stringfellows, but it's like 20 quid to get in. And it's like, yeah, we like to see naked ladies, not that much. So we went up to, I think it's called, is it Raymond's Revuebar? Do you know what I mean? It's sort of, I think it's Berwick Street or something.
Right.

And we go in there, and there's like 10 of us, and we're all dressed up in there, and we all sort of come on in. And we go, how much is it for the show? And he goes, uh, it's a tenner each for an hour-long show, various ladies, uh, stripping. Um, but it has already started. And I went, ooh, I'm not sure I want to come in now, I'm sure I won't be able to pick up the plot. And he just looked at me like, yeah, you obviously want to see the naked ladies, just come in. Pay your money, keep your mouth shut. There was no place for humour in there. So we go in, and it's not as seedy as you might think. It's actually, it's quite, quite nice in there, it's always, it's quite tasteful. It hasn't changed since about 1965, but it's okay. It's all rather like the Aberdeen Angus Steakhouse. It's not dissimilar to one of those inside. So, uh, the show's already begun, and, uh, and these girls come on. And, uh, on the outside it says, all nude girls. And there was a bloke, I swear, at the back, as the girl came on, he went, get them off!
I think that's guaranteed, to be honest.

So, um, so what was great about it was there was a kind of a voice that announced each particular girl as she came on. And she, it was so, it was so awful and camp and just ludicrous. I actually dozed off at one point, it's so boring. Because you, there's not many surprises. If you've seen one girl naked, they're all pretty much the same. There's no erotic tattoos or anything, or a slideshow hidden down there. There's nothing.
So, no puppetry.
I mean, it's just the same old thing.

So, um, so there's this voice that comes on before each girl, and it introduces her name. And they've all got amazing names. There was, uh, Scorpio Rising. Vanity Fair. Passionara Fighter. And Passionara Fighter was a girl who kind of came on straddled. They all had props. And she was straddling like a kind of anti-aircraft gun. Which is possibly the least erotic thing you can have. And as she was taking her clothes off, she sort of flung her bra off.
Steve, that sounds a bit phallic to me.
Well, I imagine it was phallic.
I've studied Freud.

And, uh, she threw her bra off, right, and it sort of, and it fell behind her. And it's a very small stage, and there's curtains at the back. And this is very hard to be erotic. When, as you see a girl's brassiere fall behind, you just see a pole with a hook on it appear from the curtains and drag it back in. And you can just see through the crack of the curtains some guys that look like when Eric Morecambe and Ernie Wise, you know, when they were trying to put that shoe back on Shirley Bassey in their classic show, where they're wearing those brown coats. It was like that, two blokes in there. But I've never been in one before, and I should never go in again. It's like, it's, I've done it now. I've done the Aberdeen Steakhouse, the paintballing, and the strip club. That's it. Three things I had to do in life before I died.
Swim with the dolphins.
Take a shower is the next one. And kiss a girl.
I saw an interesting thing last night.
Go on.
It was a repeat of a Priory with, you know, James Harries.
Who's James Harris?
You know, there's this guy, he was about ten, and he was on the Wogan show talking about antiques, and he's like...
Oh, he's like a kind of curly-haired...
Yeah, he's like a little freak boy talking about... Oh, antiques, they have to shout to you. And then he's on the Priory, and he's had a sex change.
Has he?
Yeah, yeah, he looks a bit like a young Mavis Riley now.
He's not still ten, though?
No, no, he's 20 or so.
Yeah, sure.

And they were talking about it, and they showed the clip of the Wogan thing, and there's a bit in it that goes, you're a wonderful little boy, a special little kid. I wonder what you'll be like when you're 20. And they're just thinking, well, Terry, I certainly won't have a cock, I can tell you that much. But it was great, because at one point in the Priory, he's going, yeah, he's going, you were a funny little fellow, weren't you? It was great, embarrassed, he's going, oh, yeah, he said. He said, I was worried, because at one point I thought I was gay.
Phew, that was avoided then.
I found out after I left school that one of the kids I was at school with had had a sex change, right? And a mutual friend, this is how he broke the news to me, he came in one day...
Was this one the person who had the operation?

No, no, this was another friend, he was a sort of mutual friend of ours. It wasn't a big friend, we sort of knew him, he was in our year. And my mate came round once and went, oh, yeah, he said, have you seen Darren Ripley lately? I went, er, no, no, what's he doing? He went, he's got a lovely little pair of tits. That's how I went, what? Isn't that a great way to make do? He's seen er... Lovely little pair of tits.
Did you meet him then, the sex change guy?
No.
Did you ever see him afterwards?
No, no, I haven't seen him for, yeah, 20 years.
I wonder if, cos I'm kind of intrigued now to know...
Imagine that, imagine that.
Break it to your mum, all right, hello, yeah, I was university, good, good. Can I borrow your bra?

I'm not sure I'd have had a tiny little pair of tits, I'd have had some big Jordan style ones if I had a sex change operation. Cos then I can get... No, cos then, you know, it's sort of, it's a novelty, you know, you get it in the paper.
Well, what you could do is you could have your bollocks inflated, you could have them removed and go, don't throw them away, don't throw them away.
Yeah, I've got a plan for them.
Yeah, go on, what are you thinking? I'm just thinking in the chestal area.
Oh, yeah, what, inflate the bollocks?
Ideally, yeah.
Could you attach some nipples, fake or otherwise?
You could utilise the penis as well, couldn't you?
What would that be for?
Well, it'd be a...
An interesting pendant.
Yeah.
